clock_dir_to: "be" + genitive counts DOWN to the named hour: "be penkių trys" is 02:55.
Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/be ("without", with the genitive);
clock_fraction_30: The spoken half hour names the COMING hour: "pusė trijų" (half of three)
is 02:30, "pusė aštuonių" is 07:30 -- hence bare_half_to + toward_hour_12h,
with the hour in the genitive.  Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pus%C4%97

marker_day_word: "d.", the standard abbreviation of "diena" closing a written date
("kovo 1 d.").  Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/diena, synonym section
marker_from: "nuo" + genitive = from / since.  Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/nuo
marker_future: "po" + genitive marks a forward offset ("po trijų dienų" = in three days).
Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/po ("after, following a certain time
marker_half: "pusė" (half) as the period noun of "first/second half of <year>".
marker_last: "praeitas" (past, last) as the backward determiner ("praeitą savaitę").
marker_next: "kitas" (the other, the next) as the forward determiner ("kitą savaitę").
marker_past: "prieš" + accusative marks a past offset ("prieš valandą" = an hour ago).
marker_since: "nuo" + genitive introduces the start of an open period.
marker_this: Demonstrative "šis" (this), used as a determiner; the bare accusative is
the ordinary in/during form ("šią savaitę" = this week).
marker_to: "iki" closes a range ("nuo birželio iki rugpjūčio").
marker_until: "iki" = until / up to.  Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/iki
marker_year_word: "metai" (year) and its standard abbreviation "m.", which follows the year
in the date form "1990 m. kovo 1 d.".  Declension: en.wiktionary.org,

unit_century: The counted noun's form keys off the numeral's last digit -- nominative
singular after a numeral ending in 1, nominative plural after 2-9,
genitive plural after 0 and 11-19 -- and the accusative is the form
"prieš" (ago) imposes, so all of them are surfaces of this unit.
